Both the civil appeals by leave are directed against the judgment and order dated 14.12.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos.2332 and 2333 of 2007 discharging the Rules. 4. Facts, relevant for disposal of the civil appeals, are that the petitioner herein as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.25 of 2001 on 16.04.2001 under section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet, for pre-emption of 1.67 acres of land appertaining to khatian no.530 and 167 respectively as co-sharer by inheritance stating, interalia, that the case land belonged to one Arjan Ullah who died leaving Abdul Motlib, Abul Hashem and Abdul Kader as successive heirs who subsequently sold out 53 decimals of land from plot no.1311 by registered sale deed dated 10.03.1964 to one Ishaque Mia.; Abdul. Motlib, Abul Hasheni sold out 30 decimals of land from plot no.1321 to the said Ishaque Mia by another registered sale deed dated 22.03.1963; Said Abdul Motlib also sold out another 15 decimals of sale deed dated 16.05.1963; Thus, Ishaque Mia became the owner of 53 decimals of land in plot no.1311 and 45 decimals in plot no.1321 who subsequently transferred the same to Mossammat Khairunnessa, step mother of the petitioner, by registered sale deed dated 27.06.1970 and thus, Mossammat Khairunnessa became the co-sharer in the respective khatians; Abdul Motlib and Abdul Kader died leaving pre-emptee-opposite-party nos.6-11 and 12-15 as the successive heirs; Mossammat Khairunnessa also claimed to have purchased 30 decimals of land from one Tayaibullah by registered sale deed dated 28.11.1964; She claimed to have purchased other properties in the said vicinity; Mossammat Khairunnessa died leaving one son, one daughter, husband Haji Jahir Box and pre-emptee nos.36-44; Said Haji Jahir Box died leaving wife preemptee no.20, 7 (seven) sons Md. Azad Box, Md. Afroz Box, pre-emptor no. l and pre-emptee opposite party nos.36-38, 6 daughters pre-emptee opposite party nos.39-44 and 2 daughters of a deceaseds daughter pre-emptee opposite nos.45 and 46; Pre-emptee opposite party nos.36-44 transferred their shares in plot no.1311 and 1321 to Azad Box and others and pre-emptee opposite no.31 by registered sale deed dated 0107.1989; The pre-emptor became the co-sharers in the case land by inheritance and also by purchase; The pre-emptor mutated his name in Mutation Case No.209 of 1 994/9 5; Cause of action arose in the middle of March 2001, when the pre-emptee opposite party no.2 disclosed that he and pre-emptee opposite party no.1 had purchased the case land from pre-emptee opposite party nos. -17; Having came to know about the same, the pre-emptor procured the certified copy of the sale deed dated 12.03.2001 wherefrom he had the definite knowledge that the pre-emptee opposite party nos.3-17 transferred the case land to pre-emptee opposite party nos.1 and 2 at a consideration of Tk.1,00,000/-; No notice was served upon the pre-emptor under section 89 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act; The case land is necessary to the pre-emptor for convenient and effective enjoyment of his existing land; if he knew about the said transfer, he would have purchased the same; Pre-emptee opposite party nos.1 and 2 are strangers to the case holding; The pre-emptor has made statutory deposit with the application for pre-emption. 

 "Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the co-petitioners did not file the pre-emption case within the stipulated time as prescribed under section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and sought pre-emption under section 96(4) of the Act. As they failed to discharge their burden of not having knowledge of the transfer till receipt of the notice under section 96(4) of the said Act, they are not entitled to get preemption and their claim for pre-emption is not maintainable. But the High Court Division though found that the co- petitioners failed to prove their knowledge of the alleged transfer, discharged the Rules in order to give benefit to the co-petitioners and as such the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He further submits that in sub-section 6 of section 96 of the SAT Act the phrase "whichever is earlier" is used in place. of the phrase "whichever is later" used in section 26F(4) (a) of the Bengal Tenancy Act,1885 and which goes to suggest that the pre-emption case has to be filed within 4 months of the knowledge of transfer of the land in question which was made on 12.03.2001 and the co-petitioner applied for impleading them as co-petitioners and claimed pre-emption on 07.07.2003 without stating anything about their knowledge of trans-fer and, therefore, in view of the phrase "whichever is earlier" used in section 96(4) of the SAT. Act, their claim for pre-emption is hopelessly barred by limitation. But the High Court Division misconstrued the provision of law and erroneously discharged the Rules. The learned Advocate also submits that the High Court Division committed an error in holding that section 96 (4) of the SAT Act excludes the prescribed period of limitation given in section 96(1) of the said Act in order to give benefit to the co-petitioner inasmuch as the right of pre-emption is a statutory right and unless one comes within strict compliance of law, he is not entitled to claim such right and there is no scope for giving benefit against the law and as such the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He lastly submits that the High Court Division erred in law in holding that cross objection is maintainable against the order passed in a pre-emption case. Order 41 Rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure pro-vides for filing of cross objection, only against decree, and order passed in pre-emption case is not a decree and it is only an appealable order in view of section 96(3) of the SAT Act and, therefore cross objection against an order passed in pre-emption case is not at all maintain-able. As such the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside." 

 17. From the above quoted provisions of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, it is clear that section 96 contemplates two distinct applications, one application under sub-section (1) and another application by the co-petitioner under sub-section (4) to join with the original application under sub-section (1) within the period of limitation as provided in sub-section (4) of section 96 of the Act. The right to purchase the land transferred as contemplated under section 96 is a statutory right and this right can be exercised by two ways: one is under sub-section (1) and another under subsection (4) of section 96. Under sub-section (1) this right is to be exercised within four months of the service of the notice given under section 89, or if no notice has been served under section 89, within four months of the date of knowledge of the transfer. Again, sub-section (4) provides the period of limitation for the remaining co-sharer tenants or tenants holding land contiguous to the land transferred, to join in the pre-emption proceedings, under sub-section (4) this right is to be exercised within the period referred to in sub-section (1) of section 96 of the Act or within two months of the date of the service of the notice of the application under clause (b) of sub-section (3), whichever is earlier. 

 18. It is admitted that notice under section 89 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 was not served upon the pre-emptor as well as the opposite party nos. 54-57 i.e. co-petitioners, It appears that the co-petitioners i.e. opposite party nos.54-57 were impleaded as a party by the pre-emptor by way of amendment of the application filed under section 96 of the Act. Thus, on perusal of the provisions of section 96 of the SAT Act, it is apparent that the period of limitation for the co-petitioners for filing application under sub-section (4) is two months from the service of the notice under clause (b) of sub-section (3) of section 96 i.e. the application for pre-emption.

That the pre-emptors had deposited the requisite amount of money for the purpose of pre-emption and filed the suit.

Mr. Prober Neogi, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of appellant in both the appeals has submitted that the co-petitioners did not file the pre-emption case within the stipulated time as prescribed under section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and sought pre-emption under section 96(4) of the Act.
